label: Sequence started with a: later original-phase steps and <DEL>
explanation: Fires when the first original token is a, from step 3 up to and including the <DEL> step (t <= L). It is silent at t = 0-2 and almost never fires in the copy phase (0.1% of mass), so it stays on through the input after an initial a and turns off once the model starts outputting (the first output is a). The token being input at the current step barely matters. Magnitude: in the profile examples the activation is low at t = 3, climbs to a peak around t = 4-6, and drops a little at <DEL>. The largest activations all come from sequences starting a a, but I did not score this separately. Misses (about 26% of active steps, only 6% of mass) are weak activations, mostly in sequences where a is the second token rather than the first. Adding orig(1)==a as an alternative drops precision to 0.64, so it was left out. False positives are mainly sequences of length 3 that start with a, where the feature does not fire at t=3. Dev: P 0.99, R 0.74, F1 0.85, mass recall 0.94.

issues: The core predicate holds up on test: P 0.989, R 0.738, F1 0.845, mass recall 0.937. Phase shares agree with the explanation: copy phase holds 0.1% of mass, <DEL> 17%, and t = 0-2 never fire. The activation mass by t peaks at t = 4-5 (0.27 and 0.24), which matches the magnitude claim.

One factual claim is wrong. The explanation says false positives are 'mainly sequences of length 3 that start with a', but the L=3 slice scores precision 0.97, so those sequences are not the FP source. The actual systematic FP class is 'a ? a' (a at positions 0 and 2) at exactly t = 3. The predicate (first_tok==a)&(orig(2)==a)&(t==3) has precision 0.0: the feature is fully silent there. Excluding that class raises precision from 0.989 to 0.996 at the same recall.
Also related: when the previous input is a again (prev_tok==a), precision drops to 0.77. So the feature is partly suppressed when a reappears in the input, not only at t = 3.

The claim that 'the largest activations all come from sequences starting a a' is unsupported. Sequences starting a a carry only 4.6% of activation mass (precision 0.995, recall 0.025). The magnitude ordering could not be checked with these binary scores, and that part was hedged anyway.

The misses are one systematic class: sequences with a as the second token but not the first. Restricted to t >= 4, that class has precision 0.37, recall 0.21 and mass 5.8%. The explanation already admits it, it is weak, and adding it lowers F1, so it is not a blocker.
A secondary miss pattern appeared at t = 3 with no a anywhere, often with h as the third token (prev_tok h shows 2.4x lift). It is tiny: (orig(2)==h)&(t==3) has precision 0.23 and 1.3% of mass.
